articles.title: China is putting ecosystems on the road to recovery
articles.titleCn: 中国正推动生态系统走上恢复之路
articles.summary: China is putting ecosystems on the road to recovery
articles.summaryCn: 中国通过山水林田湖草沙一体化保护和系统治理、以自然恢复为主的方针以及国际合作，推动生态系统恢复并为全球生物多样性保护作出贡献。

The article reflects the authors' opinions, and not necessarily those of CGTN. The UN biodiversity conference, COP17, marks the first major checkpoint to evaluate how countries have moved from biodiversity pledges to practice – exactly what the theme, "Taking Action for Nature," calls for. For China, the results are already in the ground.

Over several decades, China has expanded forest resources, advanced grassland restoration, strengthened wetland protection and fought {{4}}. These efforts have contributed to global greening and improved soil conservation and carbon {{5}}. They have also shaped an approach that treats nature as a unified web, not isolated patches. At its heart is the idea that mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts form an {{6}} community of life.
paragraphs.cn: 其生态修复方法为这一努力提供了模式：将相连的景观纳入协调管理，增强自然恢复能力，并通过国际合作分享知识。几十年来，中国扩大了森林资源，推进了草原恢复，加强了湿地保护并开展了防沙治沙。这些努力促进了全球绿化，改善了土壤保持和碳汇。它们还形成了一种将自然视为统一网络而非孤立斑块的方法。其核心思想是：山、水、林、田、湖、草、沙构成一个相互联系的生命共同体。

paragraphs.en:
Restoration is planned at the river basin and landscape scale, taking account of water and soil resources and drawing on cooperation across regions and government departments. Water flows, {{7}} and nutrients move, and animals {{8}} – all of which link habitats. Planning around these connections helps local projects support the functioning of a wider region, bringing land use decisions and the recovery of ecological processes into a common framework. Working with nature
In the headwaters of the Oujiang River in east China's Zhejiang Province, restoring terraces alongside traditional farming connects mountain conservation with agricultural production. In the Yellow River Delta, controlling {{9}} plants and reopening tidal channels creates conditions for native species to recover.
paragraphs.cn: 恢复工作以流域和景观尺度进行规划，考虑水土资源，并依托跨区域、跨政府部门的合作。水流、泥沙和养分移动，动物迁徙——所有这些都将栖息地联系起来。围绕这些联系进行规划，有助于地方项目支撑更广泛区域的功能，将土地利用决策和生态过程恢复纳入共同框架。与自然合作：在中国东部浙江省瓯江源头，修复梯田并与传统农业相结合，将山地保护与农业生产联系起来。在黄河三角洲，控制入侵植物并重新打通潮汐通道，为本地物种恢复创造条件。

paragraphs.en: Both examples show how practical interventions can work with natural processes. The Three-North Shelterbelt Forest Program illustrates the value of continuity. Through long-term planning, it brings sand control, water management and land restoration into a sustained effort. Together, landscape planning, continued investment and locally tailored measures tie individual projects to regional conservation goals. Wetland conservation at Namtso in Xizang Autonomous Region, southwest China.
paragraphs.cn: 两个例子都表明，实际干预措施可以与自然过程协同发挥作用。三北防护林体系建设工程体现了连续性的价值。通过长期规划，它将防沙治沙、水资源管理和土地恢复纳入持续努力。景观规划、持续投资和因地制宜的措施共同将单个项目与区域保护目标联系起来。中国西南西藏自治区纳木错的湿地保护。

paragraphs.en:
/Liu Jiakai
Minimal intervention for ecosystem self-recovery
As restoration advances, greater emphasis is being placed on ecosystem quality, ecological {{10}} and lasting resilience. Climate change, extreme weather and human activity continue to alter the conditions for recovery. Biodiversity conservation, ecosystem functions and the capacity for self-renewal must be addressed together, so restored ecosystems can adapt, withstand disturbance and continue providing services. This calls for combining targeted intervention with natural recovery. Our team has proposed an approach we call "minimal intervention for ecosystem self-recovery." It explores how identifying key barriers to recovery and intervening at the right places, at the right times and with appropriate intensity can help ecosystems regain their capacity to organize and repair themselves.
paragraphs.cn: /刘佳凯 以最小干预促进生态系统自我恢复 随着恢复工作推进，人们更加重视生态系统质量、生态完整性和持久韧性。气候变化、极端天气和人类活动持续改变恢复条件。生物多样性保护、生态系统功能和自我更新能力必须统筹应对，使恢复后的生态系统能够适应变化、抵御干扰并持续提供服务。这要求将针对性干预与自然恢复相结合。我们的团队提出了一种称为“以最小干预促进生态系统自我恢复”的方法。它探索如何识别恢复的关键障碍，并在正确的地点、正确的时间以适当强度进行干预，帮助生态系统恢复自我组织和自我修复的能力。

paragraphs.en:
Putting these ideas into practice requires integrated observation, research into ecological mechanisms and ongoing evaluation. Restoration planning should account for water availability and soil conditions, keeping interventions within local ecological limits. Cooperation across regions, sustained funding and long-term {{11}} can connect scientific research with implementation and {{12}} management, allowing measures to change as ecosystems respond. Native Suaeda salsa restoration at a site where the invasive Spartina alterniflora has been removed, Yellow River Estuary, Dongying, Shandong Province, east China. /Ning Zhonghua
Sharing the playbook
China also contributes to global conservation through practical experience, joint research and capacity building.
paragraphs.cn: 将这些理念付诸实践需要综合观测、生态机制研究和持续评估。恢复规划应考虑水资源可用性和土壤条件，使干预措施保持在当地生态限度内。跨区域合作、持续资金和长期管护可以将科学研究与实施和适应性管理联系起来，使措施能够随着生态系统响应而变化。在中国东部山东省东营黄河口，移除入侵互花米草后进行的本地盐地碱蓬恢复。 /宁中华 分享经验方案 中国还通过实践经验、联合研究和能力建设为全球保护作出贡献。

paragraphs.en: The Shan-Shui Initiative, recognized among the UN's first World Restoration Flagships, offers lessons in coordinating large-scale restoration over the long term. Along China's Yellow Sea and Bohai Gulf coast, World Heritage wetlands connect local habitat management with conservation across the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. At Tiaozini in Yancheng, east China's Jiangsu Province, the managed "720" high-tide roost gives waterbirds a place to rest when rising tides cover their feeding grounds. Protecting such sites helps sustain a migration route extending far beyond China's borders. In Mauritania, where straw is scarce, Chinese researchers and local partners adapted sand {{14}} techniques to local conditions, combining nylon sand barriers with water-saving irrigation and training in maintenance and operation.
paragraphs.cn: 被认定为联合国首批世界恢复旗舰项目的“山水工程”，为长期协调大规模恢复提供了经验。在中国黄海和渤海湾沿岸，世界遗产湿地将地方栖息地管理与东亚—澳大利西亚迁飞区保护联系起来。在中国东部江苏省盐城条子泥，受管理的“720”高潮位栖息地在涨潮淹没觅食地时为水鸟提供休息场所。保护此类地点有助于维持远远超出中国边界的迁徙路线。在秸秆稀缺的毛里塔尼亚，中国研究人员和当地伙伴根据当地条件调整固沙技术，将尼龙沙障与节水灌溉以及维护和运行培训相结合。

paragraphs.en: Sharing technical knowledge alongside practical skills helps build the capacity to sustain the work. The value lies in developing solutions with local partners and equipping them to manage those solutions over time. The International Mangrove Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, provides another platform for research exchanges and international training, supporting cooperation on coastal ecosystem conservation and restoration. Such partnerships bring experience from different regions into shared efforts to protect biodiversity. They also create opportunities to compare methods and learn how different landscapes respond to restoration.
paragraphs.cn: 在传授实用技能的同时分享技术知识，有助于建设持续开展工作的能力。其价值在于与当地伙伴共同制定解决方案，并使他们具备长期管理这些解决方案的能力。位于中国南部广东省深圳的国际红树林中心提供了另一个研究交流和国际培训平台，支持沿海生态系统保护和恢复合作。此类伙伴关系将不同地区的经验纳入保护生物多样性的共同努力。它们还创造了比较方法并了解不同景观如何响应恢复的机会。

paragraphs.en: China exchanges ideas and practical approaches at meetings of the wetlands and biodiversity conventions, as well as the Global Ecological Governance (Nansen) Conference, Asia Philanthropy Forum and Zhongguancun Forum. The Flyway University Alliance extends these exchanges into {{15}} research, monitoring and training. Chinese youth representatives have also brought stories of conservation on the ground to the global stage. These efforts give practical meaning to COP17's call for action. By connecting integrated restoration, scientific inquiry and international cooperation, China can contribute to lasting biodiversity gains and stronger ecosystem functions, while helping develop approaches suited to different environments and needs.
paragraphs.cn: 中国在湿地和生物多样性公约会议以及全球生态治理（南森）大会、亚洲公益论坛和中关村论坛等会议上交流理念和实践方法。迁飞区大学联盟将这些交流扩展到合作研究、监测和培训。中国青年代表也将基层保护故事带上全球舞台。这些努力赋予COP17行动呼吁以实际意义。通过将综合恢复、科学探究和国际合作联系起来，中国可以为持久的生物多样性增益和更强的生态系统功能作出贡献，同时帮助制定适合不同环境和需求的方法。

Editor's note: As the UN biodiversity conference, COP17, calls for turning global commitments into action, ecosystem restoration is key to protecting biodiversity and strengthening ecological resilience. CGTN invites Zhang Zhenming, professor and vice dean of the School of Ecology and Nature Conservation under Beijing Forestry University, and associate professors Liu Jiakai and Ning Zhonghua from the same school to examine China's integrated approach to ecological restoration, its efforts to combine targeted intervention with natural recovery, and its contributions to global biodiversity conservation through international cooperation. The article reflects the authors' opinions, and not necessarily those of CGTN.
The UN biodiversity conference, COP17, marks the first major checkpoint to evaluate how countries have moved from biodiversity pledges to practice – exactly what the theme, "Taking Action for Nature," calls for.
For China, the results are already in the ground. Its ecological restoration methods offer a model for this effort: bringing connected landscapes under coordinated management, strengthening nature's capacity to recover, and sharing knowledge through international cooperation.
Over several decades, China has expanded forest resources, advanced grassland restoration, strengthened wetland protection and fought desertification. These efforts have contributed to global greening and improved soil conservation and carbon sequestration. They have also shaped an approach that treats nature as a unified web, not isolated patches.
At its heart is the idea that mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts form an interconnected community of life. Restoration is planned at the river basin and landscape scale, taking account of water and soil resources and drawing on cooperation across regions and government departments.
Water flows, sediment and nutrients move, and animals migrate – all of which link habitats. Planning around these connections helps local projects support the functioning of a wider region, bringing land use decisions and the recovery of ecological processes into a common framework.
Working with nature
In the headwaters of the Oujiang River in east China's Zhejiang Province, restoring terraces alongside traditional farming connects mountain conservation with agricultural production. In the Yellow River Delta, controlling invasive plants and reopening tidal channels creates conditions for native species to recover. Both examples show how practical interventions can work with natural processes.
The Three-North Shelterbelt Forest Program illustrates the value of continuity. Through long-term planning, it brings sand control, water management and land restoration into a sustained effort. Together, landscape planning, continued investment and locally tailored measures tie individual projects to regional conservation goals.
Wetland conservation at Namtso in Xizang Autonomous Region, southwest China. /Liu Jiakai
Minimal intervention for ecosystem self-recovery
As restoration advances, greater emphasis is being placed on ecosystem quality, ecological integrity and lasting resilience. Climate change, extreme weather and human activity continue to alter the conditions for recovery. Biodiversity conservation, ecosystem functions and the capacity for self-renewal must be addressed together, so restored ecosystems can adapt, withstand disturbance and continue providing services.
This calls for combining targeted intervention with natural recovery. Our team has proposed an approach we call "minimal intervention for ecosystem self-recovery." It explores how identifying key barriers to recovery and intervening at the right places, at the right times and with appropriate intensity can help ecosystems regain their capacity to organize and repair themselves.
Putting these ideas into practice requires integrated observation, research into ecological mechanisms and ongoing evaluation. Restoration planning should account for water availability and soil conditions, keeping interventions within local ecological limits. Cooperation across regions, sustained funding and long-term stewardship can connect scientific research with implementation and adaptive management, allowing measures to change as ecosystems respond.
Native Suaeda salsa restoration at a site where the invasive Spartina alterniflora has been removed, Yellow River Estuary, Dongying, Shandong Province, east China. /Ning Zhonghua
Sharing the playbook
China also contributes to global conservation through practical experience, joint research and capacity building. The Shan-Shui Initiative, recognized among the UN's first World Restoration Flagships, offers lessons in coordinating large-scale restoration over the long term.
Along China's Yellow Sea and Bohai Gulf coast, World Heritage wetlands connect local habitat management with conservation across the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. At Tiaozini in Yancheng, east China's Jiangsu Province, the managed "720" high-tide roost gives waterbirds a place to rest when rising tides cover their feeding grounds. Protecting such sites helps sustain a migration route extending far beyond China's borders.
In Mauritania, where straw is scarce, Chinese researchers and local partners adapted sand stabilization techniques to local conditions, combining nylon sand barriers with water-saving irrigation and training in maintenance and operation. Sharing technical knowledge alongside practical skills helps build the capacity to sustain the work. The value lies in developing solutions with local partners and equipping them to manage those solutions over time.
The International Mangrove Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, provides another platform for research exchanges and international training, supporting cooperation on coastal ecosystem conservation and restoration.
Such partnerships bring experience from different regions into shared efforts to protect biodiversity. They also create opportunities to compare methods and learn how different landscapes respond to restoration.
China exchanges ideas and practical approaches at meetings of the wetlands and biodiversity conventions, as well as the Global Ecological Governance (Nansen) Conference, Asia Philanthropy Forum and Zhongguancun Forum. The Flyway University Alliance extends these exchanges into collaborative research, monitoring and training. Chinese youth representatives have also brought stories of conservation on the ground to the global stage.
These efforts give practical meaning to COP17's call for action. By connecting integrated restoration, scientific inquiry and international cooperation, China can contribute to lasting biodiversity gains and stronger ecosystem functions, while helping develop approaches suited to different environments and needs.

articles.title: Climate shocks increase health risks for Africa's most vulnerable
articles.titleCn: 气候冲击加剧非洲最脆弱群体的健康风险
articles.summary: Climate change is already reshaping Africa's health landscape, as rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, droughts, and floods worsen food insecurity, heighten infectious disease risks, and strain already fragile health systems.
articles.summaryCn: 气候变化正通过粮食不安全、疾病风险增加和流离失所等多重途径，严重威胁非洲最脆弱群体的健康与福祉，亟需加强气候适应和卫生系统建设。

articles.fullText:
Climate change is already reshaping Africa's health landscape, as rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, droughts, and floods worsen food insecurity, heighten infectious disease risks, and strain already fragile health systems.
These impacts are felt most acutely by vulnerable communities, making climate action and resilient health systems essential to safeguarding Africa's future.
John Wafula, a Humanitarian Specialist at the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) in Kenya, says the effects of climate change extend beyond environmental damage, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations and their access to essential healthcare and support.
Across Africa, many households depend on rain-fed agriculture for food and income.
When climate shocks destroy crops, livestock and other productive assets, families can lose years of hard work, deepening poverty and leaving them uncertain about their future.
Climate variability also compounds existing public health risks. Flooding can contaminate water supplies and increase exposure to waterborne diseases, while drought reduces access to safe water and compromises sanitation and hygiene. Changes in temperature and rainfall patterns can also influence the distribution of disease burden across the continent.
The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that climate change could cause approximately 250,000 additional deaths annually between 2030 and 2050 from undernutrition, malaria, diarrhoeal diseases and heat stress alone.
A mother prepares corn in Northern Kenya, July 22, 2022. 
Women and vulnerable groups face growing risks
However, the effects of climate change are not felt equally. Women and girls, older persons, persons with disabilities, refugees and other displaced populations may face additional barriers to accessing essential services and support.
Wafula says the collapse of livelihoods can push some women into harmful coping mechanisms, including transactional sex work, increasing their exposure to exploitation, violence and sexual health risks. "Such circumstances can compound psychological distress, particularly when protection services and healthcare are inaccessible," he says.
Across Africa, prolonged droughts can force women and girls to travel longer distance in search of water, increasing their exposure to insecurity and potential violence.
According to the World Bank's 2025 paper on women and climate adaptation, women face several barriers to adopting climate-smart agriculture, including insecure land tenure, limited access to climate information and greater risk aversion driven by economic vulnerability.
Limited access to information also contributes to women’s low uptake of weather insurance, while their exposure to risks, including health shocks associated with fertility and childcare, further compounds these challenges.
Household responsibilities also restrict their participation in off-farm activities, limiting opportunities for income diversification and migration in response to climate shocks.
Climate change is intensifying displacement
Furthermore, environmental pressures often intersect with conflict, insecurity and poverty, forcing families across Africa to leave their homes in search of safety and livelihoods. This creates another vulnerable population: people displaced by climate-related shocks and their compounding effects.
Wafula says climate change has contributed to the displacement of people seeking refuge in Kenya, particularly in the Dadaab and Kakuma refugee camps in northern Kenya.
"The majority of the population that arrived in the Dadaab and Kakuma refugee camps in the last five years are as a result of climate change in their respective countries. Food insecurity, limited access to healthcare and heightened protection risks are driving many from their native lands into Kenya as climate refugees," he says.
Wafula adds that between 2021 and 2025, the refugee population in the Dadaab and Kakuma camps in northern Kenya increased significantly. According to the UNHCR Portal, Kenya hosted 879,452 refugees and asylum seekers as of September 30, 2026.
These displacement trends reflect broader climate-related challenges across the region.
Climate change has largely been treated as an environmental issue, yet its consequences extend to the social, psychological and economic aspects of people's lives, undermining their sense of security, dignity and control over their lives.
Treating climate change exclusively as an environmental concern risk overlooking its far- reaching implications for health, protection and access to essential services across the region.
Wafula argues that this calls for a shift in perspective, with climate change recognized as a human rights issue and healthcare placed at the center of climate adaptation planning.
Doctors assessing malnourished children in Gulu, Uganda, November 21, 2011. 
Strengthening health systems through data and climate finance
Effective climate preparedness depends on reliable data to identify vulnerable populations, map healthcare infrastructure and anticipate emerging risks. Across the region, governments collaborate with international partners on climate data initiatives.
However, limited investment in domestic data collection and coordination risks weakening early warning systems and delaying emergency responses.
Wafula emphasizes the importance of data-driven preparedness in strengthening responses to climate-related risks.
"Governments need interoperable information systems that integrate demographic, health, environmental and population movement data. Predictive analytics can help authorities identify high-risk communities, pre-position medical supplies and allocate resources before climate-related hazards escalate into disasters," he said.
Kenya hosted the Africa Climate Summit and Africa Climate Week in 2023, creating opportunities to advance continental climate action. The Nairobi Declaration called for greater international support and increased climate financing to address Africa's vulnerabilities.
Although international climate financing, including support through the Green Climate Fund, presents opportunities to strengthen adaptation, Africa is yet to fully translate these commitments into practical health interventions.
The WHO warns that areas with weak health infrastructure, particularly in developing countries, will be least equipped to cope with climate-related health risks without support to prepare for and respond to these challenges.

(ECNS) -- General Motors' cancellation of a major supply deal has dealt a blow to U.S. rare-earth ambitions.
GM, the biggest customer of a U.S. factory making rare-earth magnets for electric vehicles, canceled its long-term supply deal with the manufacturer, Reuters reported recently.
Last November, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stood inside a rare-earth permanent magnet plant in Sumter, South Carolina, holding up a neodymium-iron-boron magnet. Speaking to Fox Business, he said that this was the first magnet manufactured in the U.S. in 25 years, adding that “we’re ending China’s chokehold on our supply chain.”
One year later, however, the plant’s biggest customer — GM, which accounted for 90% of its orders — has walked away from a 10-year supply agreement, dealing a major blow to the project, Reuters reported.
The plant, with an investment of about $500 million and an annual production capacity of nearly 2,000 metric tons, is owned by German magnet maker Vacuumschmelze, or VAC. GM and VAC announced plans to build the facility in the U.S. in 2021 and signed a long-term supply agreement in 2023.
In effect, the factory was built around the prospect of supplying GM for a decade. With its biggest customer now pulling out, the value of a facility once touted as a strategic U.S. industrial asset has taken a serious hit.
GM’s decision to withdraw, however, was also a move to protect its own business.
VAC had been willing to place nearly all its eggs in one basket because it counted on the U.S. government to support the project. This was no ordinary commercial venture, but a strategic asset fostered by government subsidies and policy support.
In its early operating phase, the plant received funding from the Pentagon, as well as $111.9 million in tax credits under the qualifying advanced energy project credit program, according to a Goldinvest report.
Apart from the 90% of output earmarked for GM, almost all the remaining 10% was intended for the U.S. government, VAC told Reuters.
The magnets reserved under the 10-year agreement were originally intended for motors in GM electric vehicles. But after taking office in 2025, the Trump administration rolled back federal incentives and tax credits for electric vehicles. GM’s electric vehicle business has long been unprofitable, and with those subsidies gone, cutting output was a rational choice.
Even if GM had honored the agreement, would that have been enough to establish a self-sufficient U.S. rare-earth industry? Not necessarily. The challenge facing the U.S. supply chain is not simply securing orders, but ensuring consistent delivery at competitive costs and acceptable quality.
The real barriers in the rare-earth industry lie not in mining, but in the expertise required for separation and magnet manufacturing.
Marina Yue Zhang, an associate professor at the Australia-China Relations Institute at the University of Technology Sydney, said core technological knowledge resides not just in equipment but in the decades of process experience and knowledge held by engineers, according to The Star.
In the 1990s, the U.S. moved much of its rare earth processing overseas because of high environmental compliance costs and low profit margins. Now, rebuilding a domestic rare earth supply chain means training a new generation of skilled workers from the ground up.
Gavin Harper, a critical materials research fellow at the University of Birmingham, told The Star that specialist skills in rare earth separation, metal making and alloy production had atrophied as knowledge withered.
“It is not only [the] operating processes that need to be rebuilt but also the knowledge of how to manufacture the machinery and equipment to create those processes from scratch that needs to be rebuilt,” Harper said.
Capital can finance the construction of a magnet plant within a few years. Building a workforce of engineers capable of keeping the production line running reliably, however, could take a long time.
Even if the U.S. can gradually make up for its technological and talent gaps, domestically produced magnets still face a major obstacle in the marketplace: cost.
According to data from Fudan Development Institute, producing one kilogram of medium-grade neodymium-iron-boron magnets costs about $26 in China, compared with around $34 in the U.S. and other Western countries — a difference of roughly 30%. Chinese manufacturers also typically operate on thin profit margins of less than 10%, relying on high-volume sales. By contrast, new U.S. projects require profit margins of around 30% to attract investment. As a result, the price gap for finished products could reach as much as 80%.
Government contracts and guaranteed high prices may sustain a limited amount of American domestic production. But civilian markets are unlikely to pay a premium simply for a product’s country of origin. GM’s withdrawal is a case in point.
A White House executive order requires U.S. defense contractors and other manufacturers to stop purchasing rare-earth magnets, tungsten, molybdenum, tantalum and other critical materials from China, Russia, Iran and North Korea starting Jan. 1, 2027.

A television station broadcasts Anthropic IPO news on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange in New York, US, October 26, 2026. 
US artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic publicly filed its prospectus for an initial public offering (IPO) on Monday, which could become the largest stock market debut in history.
The filing, a registration statement on Form S-1 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, did not set the number of shares to be sold or a price range. Anthropic intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT, according to a release on the company's website.
Both the company and existing shareholders will sell shares, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley named first among 24 underwriters. The company is expected to begin trading in mid-November, and backers hope for a valuation of up to $2 trillion, though some investors have weighed a figure closer to $1.5 trillion, according to Reuters.
A news ticker displays Anthropic IPO news on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange in New York, US, October 26, 2026. 
The prospectus offers the first detailed look at the finances of the developer of the Claude AI models. Revenues reached $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.16 billion year on year, after growing from $41 million in 2023 to $386 million in 2024 and $4.59 billion in 2025. Revenues in the second quarter alone were $11.56 billion, and the company reported its first quarterly operating profit of $974 million.
The headline losses are far larger, but most stem from accounting charges rather than cash spending. Anthropic recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, of which $72.4 billion came from changes in the fair value of convertible notes and other instruments as the company's own valuation climbed. Its operating loss for the period was $693 million, while operating cash flow turned positive at $3.93 billion. Cash and short-term investments totaled $131.7 billion at June 30.
The filing warns that this rapid pace may not last. "We cannot assure you [revenue] will continue to grow at all," the company said in the prospectus, which also notes it is on track for a second consecutive quarter of adjusted operating profit.
Spending on computing power remains the central cost. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing resources and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, and has committed to $518 billion in future infrastructure spending. It has agreed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon through April 2036 and at least $114.5 billion with Google through July 2033. Amazon holds $6.2 billion of notes that convert into non-voting stock, capped at 12% of the company.

Existing customers spend roughly nine times what they did a year ago, but two unnamed customers accounted for about 23% of revenues in the first half of 2026.
Public investors will be able to buy the shares but will not steer the company. A single Class F share held by the seven co-founders carries 50.1% of every stockholder vote, and a trust will elect a majority of the board. A Public Benefit Fund will hold 5% of the company in non-voting shares, and each co-founder has pledged to give 80% of their personal Anthropic equity to philanthropic causes.

AI部门实现营业利润4.31亿美元，而去年同期亏损17亿美元。与其他AI公司一样，支出仍然沉重。SpaceX本季度投资196亿美元，其中164亿美元用于AI，使今年前九个月的资本支出达到480亿美元。其计算能力达到1.7吉瓦，高于去年同期的0.6吉瓦。马斯克表示，他“相当有信心”SpaceX能在2027年再上线10吉瓦的计算能力。

这将是在预计到今年年底将投入运行的约2.5至3.0吉瓦的基础上增加的。他补充说，电力、冷却和电气设备是“某种程度上限制因素”。星链卫星互联网部门营收增长69%，至52亿美元，消费者用户达到1360万。然而，每用户平均月收入从去年同期的83美元降至69美元。SpaceX还完成了星舰的首次创收飞行，这枚巨型火箭对马斯克的火星雄心以及大规模部署卫星至关重要。
